05b0205b.text: Detention. Again. Apparently I "electrocuted" the vending machine.

86858276.text: It's not my fault metal sparks when I touch it. Nothing about me is ever my fault.

c0d40b54.text: …Seventeen years, and the storms still follow me everywhere.

18d32609.text: Ariel Stormborn. Do you have any idea how hard you are to find? Seventeen years of searching!

d6b11c42.text: Who are you? How did you get up here? Are those… wings on your shoes?

1bd2d5a3.text: Hermes. Messenger of the gods. Patron of travelers, thieves, and very late deliveries.

09b1160c.text: Your father sent me. Well — what is left of him.

f83d6d36.text: My father walked out before I was born.

0f4d4c09.text: Your father is Zeus, King of Olympus. And right now, Olympus is dying.

b519c113.text: Kronos has corrupted the gods. Ares, Athena, Poseidon — all of them. Only the blood of Zeus can reclaim their stolen sparks.

153018c5.text: I have a chemistry test on Monday.

1d4e0ed5.text: Then you had better be quick. Hold still. This is going to sting.

50a84b32.text: Ugh… where…? Okay. Okay. That's a giant golden tree. That is a GIANT golden tree.

bc41930e.text: Welcome to Elysia — the Shattered Realm, where the broken pieces of Olympus come to rest.

c700b492.text: That blade is Keraunos, forged from your father's first thunderbolt. It answers only to his blood.

c2391492.text: Cool. Cool cool cool. And the mountain with the storm sitting on top of it?

d143e87c.text: Olympus. Kronos sits upon your father's throne. But you are not ready for him — not yet.

4903ecf1.text: North, past the Agora, stands the Colosseum of Ares. The God of War has fallen to the rot. Free him, and reclaim the Spark of War.

4f153d93.text: When you are hurt, rest at the Altars of Hestia. Her flame mends flesh… though it also wakes the shades you have slain.

73abb9c7.text: Shades. Ghost soldiers. Great. Love that for me.

f31f6a82.text: Go, Heir of Thunder. I will be watching. Probably from somewhere very safe.

fc5f8ab8.text: Ariel! You have eight minutes, and I have watched you lose a fight with a sock for longer than that.

57cc1220.text: I'm up. Mostly. Is that coffee?

bb66ba9b.text: It's mine. Yours is orange juice and a lecture.

7df62cc7.text: Can I skip to the juice?

cb8d8e31.text: Mrs. Patterson called. Every microscope in the science lab fried at once. While you were standing next to them.

5193f9b8.text: That's a coincidence. Electronics hate me. It's a known thing.

7d44e1b0.text: Because the answer is always "he had to go." Seventeen years, Mom. Who just goes?

67b040c8.text: …Sit down. You want to know? Then I'll tell you. All of it. Just once.

e6314f09.text: It was the summer I turned twenty. The worst storm this town has ever seen — and I was the only fool out on the old pier, watching it come in.

2ab4576e.text: He walked out of the rain like it was parting for him. He didn't run. He didn't even get wet.

0f73afb8.text: You are not afraid of the storm.

f15ca43c.text: He stayed the whole summer. I never asked where he came from. I think part of me already knew.

ca46cb7b.text: He left before you were born. And the night you came into the world, every light in the hospital went out — and he was there. Just for a moment.

c7ea3e97.text: I give you my thunder… and a heart for war that is not mine to give. Forgive me, little one. You will need them both.

14942ca9.text: When the storms come looking for him, I will send someone. Until then, keep him close. Keep him kind.

9f446262.text: Will we ever see you again?

b40a559f.text: Look up whenever it storms. That's all he left me. That, and you.

2da18d4b.text: Mom. You're telling me Dad was some kind of… weather guy.

3b2c18ed.text: I didn't say what he was.

a22717ba.text: Take the umbrella. It's going to storm.

e6ff5a55.text: Around you, it does. Now go, you'll be late. And Ariel? Be kind today.

f8db0138.text: You're late, Stormborn. Even for you.

3eeb8804.text: Is this about the microscopes? Because the whole school thinks you have a superpower. Mostly the power of breaking stuff.

25243170.text: Uh-huh. You okay? You look like someone just told you a ghost story.

390a8ec4.text: Ugh, my phone just died. Again. Every single time you stand next to me.

92912975.text: Lab partners don't let lab partners brood before first period. Buy me a soda, and I'll let you copy my chem homework.

5a6cf582.text: Come on. Come on… I literally just paid you.

09a3ef0b.text: Dude. Did you just electrocute the vending machine?

c2b329aa.text: STORMBORN! My office. Now. And after school, you can spend the evening in detention, thinking about school property.

c1e367ff.text: I'll get you that soda later.

2c83343d.text: You'd better. See you in chem, Stormborn.

aa84434e.text: Do you feel it, little brother? The war in your blood… calling home.

289d24c5.text: Who said that? Who — get out of my head!

6b4b4fe4.text: That armour. That face. Did you never wonder why they look like mine?

5276c619.text: Seventeen years ago your father cut a shard from my spark — my war, my strength — and sealed it inside a mortal child. Inside you.

66b81ab4.text: And what is mine answers to me. Kneel to war, boy.

3882b4b0.text: Hands off the boy, you overgrown war drum!

efd77414.text: He was in my head. He moved my arm. Hermes — what is he talking about?

b6a26363.text: I had hoped to have this conversation after you freed him. Or, ideally, never.

73f7b928.text: When Kronos began to stir, your father knew his thunder alone would never keep a mortal child alive. So he cut a shard from Ares' spark and sealed it in you, right beside his own.

7f587d38.text: I carried it to your cradle myself. Wrapped in a storm cloud, still burning. Ares was never asked.

417a131d.text: So the armour. The face. I don't look like a god of war… I look like him.

7a89b4b1.text: You look like the piece of him you carry. And that wound is how the rot got in. Kronos whispered that Zeus chose a mortal over his own son — and Ares believed him.

e8be6ece.text: While the rot holds him, he can reach through that shard and pull your strings. When he does, fight him. Hard. He lets go of what fights back.

a420b2bd.text: Great. My half-brother is living rent-free in my head. Just what I needed.

f425f660.text: Look on the bright side: while he has hold of you, you hit like he does. Try not to enjoy it.

0545087c.text: Another little godling, sent to die in my arena.

d05720a3.text: I am ARES. I am every war that was ever fought — and every war that ever will be.

790b57f5.text: You're also, like, the size of a bus.

f7aa63ad.text: And still you wear my face, little thief. Did the messenger tell you whose strength you have been borrowing?

8d083966.text: He told me. Doesn't mean you get it back.

11182b2c.text: Kronos showed me the truth, boy. Olympus is a corpse wearing a crown — and your father let it rot.

74d20f05.text: Come, son of Zeus. Show me your father's thunder — so I can tear it from your chest!

c68d6789.text: The rot… it burns away. My mind is… my own again.

f9d66a32.text: Boy. Kronos waits on Olympus, on your father's throne. Every god you free will weaken his hold.

bda62c2e.text: That shard in your chest… I hated you for it before you could walk. A mortal, wearing my strength like a borrowed cloak.

6e8e7554.text: It was never his to give. So let it be mine. Keep it, brother.

9a376fe1.text: Take my spark. Wield it better than I did.

e2a0b7ad.text: One spark returns to Olympus. Eleven remain in shadow — and each will be harder won than the last.

35fbf5b7.text: I am sorry I was not there. Rise now, Heir of Thunder. Olympus awaits.

f0861463.text: Hear me, brother. The mantle of war was never mine to keep. I wore it like a butcher wears his apron.

70523bd2.text: Take it. Be the god of war that I never was.

830174be.text: …Then I will make it mean something.

0075ba3b.text: Olympus stood again in the light, as it was in the beginning.

3492b366.text: Three days, Ariel. Three days, and not one word.

b4fa10bd.text: I met him, Mom. Dad. He said he was sorry he was not there.

20d97ea4.text: …He was always there. In every storm that ever passed over this house.

e1b837fd.text: They want me on Olympus. A throne, a mantle, all of it. I said yes.

d566c311.text: But I am not leaving you. I am not leaving any of this.

96c49566.text: Then you will do the one thing your father never could. You will be both.

6e1cc359.text: The microscopes. The lights at the dance. The bolt that missed the bus by a foot. That was you. All of it.

9bc07c8f.text: Would you believe me if I said yes?

784b1f8f.text: Stormborn, I have believed you since the third grade. Try me.

25f1cf32.text: Anna kept that photograph on her mantel for the rest of her life.

cf295e23.text: He has your eyes. And your father's weather.

f8aec782.text: A grandson. Olympus has not heard a child cry in a thousand years.

56f343ef.text: And so the son of a storm became a father, and the story of the gods began again, in the halls of Olympus, in his mother's arms.

07c4c55d.text: Dad. Ares. If you can hear me — I need everything you have.

ec78087d.text: You never needed to ask, my son. The sky has always been yours.

63e08697.text: And the war answers with it, brother. Let them see what the two of us made.

deb72ca9.text: You want my war, little thief? Then take it. Every drop. And see if you can hold it.

867c4a48.text: Before memory… before the first mortal looked up and named the stars… there was Olympus.

b50f6c32.text: Upon its summit the gods ruled sky, sea and soul. Zeus of the thunder. Poseidon of the deep. Wise Athena. And Hades, keeper of the dead.

44451bdc.text: But far below, in the black pit of Tartarus, something old was waiting. Something patient.

5d1a70a2.text: Kronos. The Devourer of Ages. A father who once swallowed his own children — and swore one day to finish the meal.

a00a79c6.text: When his chains broke, the rot came with him. It crept through the marble halls like a slow, cold tide.

8f56ef3a.text: One by one, the Olympians fell. Their divine sparks were torn from their hearts, and scattered across a shattered realm.

5e63e3fd.text: With the last of his strength, Zeus hid a single spark where Kronos would never think to look…

720e16be.text: And the Fates, who see every thread, wove what was still to come.

deaca9d9.text: The son of Zeus took up the mantle of war, and carried it into the dark places of the world.

01137801.text: One by one, the stolen sparks came home — until the Titan himself was cast down into Tartarus.

daa4013e.text: The gods walked again on Olympus: the sea-king, the grey-eyed one, the lord of the dead — and their King.

b0ad3067.text: Their fires were lit, their columns stood, and Olympus shone over the world once more.

4e6e68b9.text: And at the right hand of Zeus stood the new God of War: Ariel, Heir of Thunder.

1d8f8cd2.text: By day he was still Ariel Stormborn of Westbrook High, who turned his chemistry homework in late.

9b0d27b2.text: By night the God of War kept watch over the old places of the world, and the old places were quiet.

83ac90ae.text: He told Jesse everything: the shard, the storm, the father in the rain. She listened to the very end, and she did not run.

fa9b2f85.text: They finished school together, under a sky that held back its thunder for one whole afternoon.

64a13edb.text: Olympus stands again. And at my right hand, the God of War — my son.

6589a168.text: Zeus came as a warm summer rain. Ares came in his own fire, and for the first time it warmed instead of burned.

dc0bdc05.text: Two winters after Kratos came his brother, Deimos: dread. A red ember burned beside the blue in him, the war-god's shard come home in the blood.

305bbbf8.text: The brothers grew up between two worlds: Saturday football in Westbrook, and Sunday sword-drill on the slopes of Olympus.

81b6435a.text: Kratos had his father's strength, and Deimos his grandfather's fury. Ariel, who had carried both, taught them the one thing no god had ever learned: when not to fight.

fe2c3fc4.text: Anna grew old in the house by the sea. And every storm that ever passed over it stopped there, for a moment, to rest.

5940d272.text: This is how the story ends. Everything else is how it happens.

36f782c9.text: You actually did it! Ares is himself again — well, as pleasant as Ares ever gets.

8d2a1632.text: Need something, Heir of Thunder? Be quick, I have fourteen deliveries and a very angry centaur waiting.

e97db5d5.text: Elysia. When Kronos shattered Olympus, the pieces fell here — temples, heroes, whole fields of gold. The realm remembers everyone who walked it.

416f404e.text: Those glowing sigils on the ground? Echoes of demigods who came before you. Read them. Some are even helpful.

cbd1bfa6.text: The Titan of time. Father of Zeus — your grandfather, if you want to make family dinners awkward.

b94e7c59.text: He devoured his own children once. Now he devours their divinity instead. Every spark he steals makes him stronger.

f9b3e288.text: Even Hades. You should have seen him at court — crowned, proud, impossible. The rot burned all of that away. What rules the underworld now only wears his name.

8e741459.text: Kill shades and you collect their Ichor — the golden blood of the divine. Offer it at an Altar of Hestia to grow stronger.

dcc0ef9e.text: And find the golden apples of the Hesperides. Each one lets you carry another draught of Ambrosia.

d8f424d8.text: Because a piece of him lives in you — and now he has given it freely. The shard is yours, Ariel. The face, the strength, all of it.

31657ad3.text: He will still call you little thief, I imagine. From Ares, that is practically a hug.

b508daec.text: Because a piece of him lives in you. The shard your father sealed in your cradle shaped you in its own image — armour, face and all.

1fca9118.text: And while the rot holds him, it is a leash. Free him, and it becomes a gift. Until then, when the world goes red, fight him.

bdf6ed62.text: Athena waits in the Library of Ash, and Poseidon has drowned an entire coast in his grief. Eleven sparks remain.

ac720cb7.text: For now, rest. Explore. Even heroes need to finish their chemistry homework.

5dc278b8.text: He swings wide — roll through his blade, toward him, not away. When he lifts that sword to the sky, run. Far.

a4e726f1.text: And when he leaps, watch where he lands. Then do not be there.

1f0a74f6.text: Until the next spark, cousin. Er — half-brother. It is complicated.

c619b9dd.text: May your father's thunder guide your hand.

78364ff0.text: Stop fighting me. You were made for this.

0389da2f.text: Try rolling ▸ through the spear, not away from it.

c6a0f5d2.text: Beware the one-eyed giant… and his stomp.

d4f8f218.text: Behold, golden fruit near the fallen hero.

2c4ccd93.text: Rest at the altar ahead. Thunder answers patience.

6f565c34.text: Fire, O fire… when he lifts his blade to the sky, run.

94e09c15.text: Seven summers later, on the pier where Anna once met a stranger in the rain, Ariel married Jesse. Anna gave the bride away, and Hermes, of course, was late.
